# Preparing the private envelope node-visit experiment

This source-only experiment moves one node initialization in `insertRange`. On full coverage, the existing `insertLine` initializes the same node before arithmetic. Partial nodes retain initialization before unchanged recursion. The production Go file remains byte-for-byte e492; both Go payloads here use `.source` suffixes.

`producer.py` exposes only source preparation and bounded native unit controls. It has no module build, graph, audio, profiler or timing entry point. The Chair must release those later stages separately. Public selection and ABI remain unchanged; the whole product is **open — awaiting merge**.

## Source admission

The unchanged `extrema_screen/producer.py` source admission runs first. It checks all qualified Go/go.mod bytes, the exact tracked and ignored/untracked Go inventories, all six excluded AR files, historical native/WASM evidence bytes, and old exact 14/6 overlay maps. Nothing in those runners or proofs is modified.

The new baseline is current e492 under the existing six-file AR exclusions. The new candidate adds exactly one envelope replacement. Source preparation records both effective source sets, both historical overlay maps and hashes, the copied original control, the original Chair unit evidence hashes, and all runner hashes. Native unit overlays replace only the existing opt-in screen test with the independent control source; its physical bytes stay unchanged.

The control body is the original e492 envelope with only its receiver type renamed. Admission compares that body to the original bytes. Tests compare epochs and IEEE slope/offset bits in all 8,192 nodes after each operation, plus query bits. They cover random full/partial insertions, dirty matching/stale epochs, signed zero, subnormal, infinity and NaN payloads, extreme epoch diagnostics, physical chunk wrap, large clocks, clipped active rebuilds, and native allocation counts. These are synthetic envelope units, not graph/audio acceptance.

## Running the allowed stages

Use pinned Go 1.26.10 and Node 26.12.0 on `PATH`. All managed-worktree writes, including Go cache writes, require the authorized escalated terminal execution.

```sh
python3 internal/audio/dsp/testdata/envelope_node_visit/producer.py prepare node-visit-source-v1
python3 internal/audio/dsp/testdata/envelope_node_visit/producer.py unit node-visit-source-v1
```

Preparation and each unit run are exclusive: use a fresh ID for new evidence and preserve every earlier receipt. Each native child has a 20-second Go timeout, 25-second supervisor wall limit, 256 KiB log cap, and retained process-group cleanup result. No benchmark is selected.

## Required later evidence

Before timing, separately review and release the original alias, partition, finite-tail, repeat/reset, capacity and no-allocation gates; native fullgraph 135-case byte comparison; and actual GoJS fullgraph 135-case byte comparison. Compare both sides to the corresponding current e492 archived candidate streams at all five rates. Preserve the exact existing 200,000 base-frame, 800,000 high-rate-frame, 16 Mi numeric-word, 8 MiB output, 2 MiB graph-object, 16 MiB module and bounded-child limits.

Native/WASM numeric-state payload differences remain unproven even when PCM matches. The earlier race timeout, Node exit 1, Nyquist/33.2 kHz transparency failures, Newton limitation and unqualified AR evidence remain open. Existing steady 192 kHz means exceed 0.666666667 ms per 128 frames. The new source and synthetic controls establish no deadline, headroom, physical steady-state, EOF/drain, browser continuity or public-activation result.
